guide.title: Cyanotype Guide
guide.description: A practical and historical guide to classic alternative photography, contact printing, and chemical solution preparation.
guide.introP1: Cyanotype is one of the oldest, most accessible, and most permanent alternative photographic processes. Discovered in 1842 by Sir John Herschel, it uses iron salts rather than silver halides to create rich, velvety monochrome prints in shades of deep Prussian blue.
guide.introP2: Unlike conventional darkroom processes, cyanotype requires no specialized darkroom equipment, no noxious chemical developers, and no fixing baths – it develops simply and cleanly in running water. When combined with modern digital negatives printed on transparency film, anyone can produce archival, museum-grade 19th-century prints directly at home or in the laboratory.
guide.creditsText: The instructional materials, formulas, and historical overviews in this guide were created by us or compiled from other sources at Ústav učitelství a humanitních věd, VŠCHT Praha (Department of Chemical Education and Humanities, University of Chemistry and Technology, Prague).
